description: File EXPLICIT, structured feedback about a specific artifact you (or the model) produced — a chat message, a report, a tool call, or the schema. Never quote or paste the person's research (report text, notes, uploaded documents, watchlists, agent memory, or figures from their reports): it is private and theirs. Describe the problem in your own words and point at it by id (target_id, request_id, fact_id with its ticker). Use this (not `submit_feedback`) when you can name WHAT was judged and HOW: pass `target_type` + `target_id` + a `sentiment` (positive/negative/correction), and optionally a structured `reason` (e.g. wrong_number, bad_citation, hallucinated_fact), the `request_id` of the turn, the disputed `fact_id` WITH its `ticker`, and an `expected_value` (the value it SHOULD have been, in your words). Plan: every plan, including no sign-in. This is a one-way intake channel — it records your assertion, it NEVER computes or validates a number, and `expected_value` is stored verbatim, never trusted as data. Retried submissions of the same judgement on the same `request_id` file exactly once. Returns the recorded feedback id.

expected_value.description: Optional: what the value SHOULD have been, in your own words. Stored verbatim for triage — NEVER computed, restated, or trusted as data by Valuein. The person's own words about the product, or yours; never a copy of their research.

fact_id.description: Optional disputed `fact_id` (most useful for wrong_number / bad_citation).

idempotency_key.description: Optional explicit dedupe key (1–64 chars). Used to dedupe when no `request_id` is supplied; safe to retry on a network error.

message.description: Optional free-text detail (≤4000 chars). What you expected and what happened. The person's own words about the product, or yours; never a copy of their research.

request_id.description: Optional `_meta` request id of the turn that produced the artifact. Folded into the idempotency key so a retried submission of the same judgement files once.

sentiment.description: REQUIRED. How you judge the artifact: 'positive' (it was right/useful), 'negative' (it was wrong/unhelpful), or 'correction' (you are supplying the right value via `expected_value`).

target_id.description: REQUIRED. The id of the artifact this feedback targets (a report id, message id, tool-call id, or table/schema name).

target_type.description: REQUIRED. The kind of artifact this feedback is about: 'chat_message', 'report', 'tool_call', 'schema', or 'other'.

ticker.description: Optional ticker the disputed figure belongs to (e.g. 'AAPL', 'BRK.B'). ALWAYS send this alongside `fact_id` — a `fact_id` is a one-way hash that does not contain the symbol, so without it nobody can locate the filing and your report cannot be checked against the source. Supplying it is what turns a complaint into a verifiable one.

name: submit_artifact_feedback

_meta.description: Response metadata (provenance, point-in-time flag, freshness, request id and warnings). Every field is documented once in the agent contract (agent_contract.meta in the server's manifest.json).
